notes.166.1: Usermaatre-setepenre is Ramesses II. Line 2 is largely obscure: the opening names are foreign-sounding magical names and their vocalisation is a guess; wdḥ 'pour out', ḫr.tw (taken as 'before'), and jmm! (marked by the editor; perhaps 'give') are all uncertain, and the syntax of the whole line is doubtful. 'The one who killed his brother' is presumably Seth.

nodes.text: The book that was found at the throat of King Usermaatre-setepenre, may he live, prosper and be healthy, in the necropolis.

O Werbeg, O Kemmer, O Amag, O Kerkhem, O Kemry, Nyunermet, you who pour out (offerings) before Ra and the Aten, to present to them what is ... upon you for the mourner, since he died in want, the one who killed his brother.
